clue.text: Busy fellow, the archdeacon, though at heart a composer

parts.note: a bee is the proverbially busy creature
tho' is the old short spelling of though
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A clergyman who bustles about yet secretly dreams of writing symphonies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' links the wordplay to the definition: the busy archdeacon is a composer at heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig van Beethoven is among the most celebrated German composers of symphonies.

clue.text: Dorset poet carries one to the singers

indicators.note: a poet who carries something holds it within himself, so the letters go inside

parts.note: William Barnes wrote poems in Dorset dialect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A West Country poet brings someone along to the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is a county in south-west England; William Barnes is its best-known dialect poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Male voices pitched between tenor and bass are a class of singers.

clue.text: As Cervantes said, the end of fairies?

definitions.meaning: in Spanish, the language of Cervantes
an adjective meaning like or belonging to the little people

explanation.surface: Spanish literature meets the death of fairyland.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two Spanish words, EL FIN, and it is what a Spanish author would write for 'the end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish el fin translates 'the end'; elfin describes things relating to elves and other little people.

clue.text: Top mark-coming first in the exam paper perhaps

definitions.text: coming first in the exam paper perhaps

parts.note: the head is the top of something
a note is a mark or written annotation

explanation.surface: Earning the best grade by being first to finish the examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief summary placed at the top of a document or exam paper, preceding the main text.

clue.text: Part of army vehicle used by a drug combine

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

indicators.note: to combine is to mix together, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A military truck is commandeered by a narcotics syndicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' rearranges A DRUG into GUARD, placed after VAN; 'used by' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading section of an advancing force, the troops at the front.

clue.text: Spirit of Pooter ?

definitions.meaning: a ghost has no corporeal form, so read as two words it is a being without flesh
Charles Pooter is the hero of the Grossmiths' The Diary of a ...

explanation.surface: Asking about the ghost of a famous fictional diarist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is a classic English comic novel narrated by the self-important clerk Charles Pooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost is a being lacking flesh, read as two words; Pooter is the insignificant person of the book's title.

clue.text: Country, if backward, has Jolly good railways

indicators.note: the letters for both pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with I for 1
Ry is the abbreviation for railway, so Rys for railways

explanation.surface: A nation that, looked at in reverse, boasts excellent trains.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of A1 is taken as the letter I; turned round, AI and RYS give the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation with Damascus as its capital.

clue.text: Honest bribe ?

definitions.meaning: to pay someone off so they keep quiet, a verb

explanation.definitionFit: A fair, upright dealer is said to be on the level; to buy off an official is to fix him with money.

clue.text: Sets of criminals, perhaps

definitions.meaning: radio or television sets that pick up broadcasts

explanation.surface: A description of gangs of lawbreakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Radios and televisions pick up signals; fences who take stolen goods are guilty of handling them.

clue.text: Specimen for beheading that's quite enough!

indicators.note: beheading removes the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a sample is a specimen taken for testing

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that one more execution victim is plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for beheading' drops the first letter, S, from SAMPLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful, more than sufficient for the purpose.

clue.text: Forbear to be a burden?

definitions.meaning: to hold back from doing something
the burden of a song is its recurring chorus

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid being a nuisance to others.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to hold back; the repeated chorus of a song is called its burden.

clue.text: Bird's achievements in games?

definitions.meaning: a name for the blue tit, the 's standing for 'is'
at Oxford and Cambridge a blue is awarded for sport, and a cap for playing for one's country

explanation.surface: Wondering about a bird's sporting successes.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue is awarded at Oxford or Cambridge for representing the university at sport; a cap is given for a national team appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect name for the blue tit; the two words are sporting honours, a university blue and an international cap.

clue.text: Bit of carpentry-or some music in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a nonet is a composition for nine players

explanation.surface: A joiner's work, or else a tune played after leaving the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting piece of wood cut to fit a mortise in a joint.

clue.text: Stress makes us break rule in end

indicators.note: breaking the words up lets their letters be reassembled

explanation.surface: Emphasising a point causes us to flout the regulations at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges RULE IN END; 'makes us' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise, as by drawing a line beneath words in a text.

clue.text: Worthless weapon returned by a politician

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A useless firearm handed back by a member of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Of no value or force, trifling or invalid.

clue.text: Boastful talk of the fuel business Dean organized

parts.note: gas is a fuel
Co is short for company, a business

indicators.note: organizing puts things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman's bragging about the energy company he set up.
explanation.definitionFit: Extravagant bragging, from the Gascons' reputation for boasting.

clue.text: Whip round?

parts.note: the rounded part of the body a whipping is aimed at, punning on a collection among colleagues

explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks, the round part of the body that a flogging lands on.

clue.text: School is not up to game

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: An institution that falls short of the standard required for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NOT into TON; 'is' links. Tonbridge School is an English public school in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: An independent boys' school in Kent, England, founded in 1553.

clue.text: Rather tame show perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints at another possible arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A dull performance, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: To some degree, fairly or moderately.

clue.text: An ornament or two permitted

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
let means allowed

explanation.surface: Being allowed one or two pieces of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative band or chain worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Band remains after start of show

indicators.note: after puts the remains following the opening letter
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A group of musicians stays on after the concert begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

clue.text: .Poet gets no backing from labour statesman

parts.note: William Morris was a Victorian poet and designer

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: A versifier gets no support from a Labour politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NO into ON. Herbert Morrison was a leading British Labour Party politician of the 1940s.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbert Morrison was a senior Labour cabinet minister and deputy prime minister under Attlee.

clue.text: Tale was first to include the information

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside

parts.note: to have led is to have been in front
gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: A story that was the first to carry the news.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional story, popularly regarded as historical but unverified.

clue.text: Score over that poetic American writer

parts.note: in cricket or baseball a run is a score
yon is a poetic word for that

explanation.surface: Twenty times over that verse-writing American author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' simply links in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Damon Runyon wrote short stories of Broadway gamblers and gangsters.

clue.text: Follow up with writing attractive to Americans

parts.note: prose is ordinary writing
cute means attractive in American English

explanation.surface: Pursuing the matter with appealing text for US readers.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue or carry on a course of action, as with prosecuting a war.

clue.text: Cracked-as description of earthenware vessels?

definitions.meaning: a jocular adjective for pots, like pots

explanation.surface: Wondering about damaged pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for crazy; jokily, made of or resembling pots.

clue.text: Polish participant in Highland games?

parts.note: seems a competitor from Poland at a Scottish sports meeting, but is a pole tossed there

explanation.definitionFit: The tree trunk that competitors toss at Scottish games is a sort of pole.

clue.text: Cheerful villain?

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of cheering, read as a word of applause

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bad guy is in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of approval, a cheer; also an old word for a hired thug or assassin.

clue.text: Attempt to include old play, perhaps

parts.note: a try is an attempt
aged means old

explanation.surface: Trying to put on a dated drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama with an unhappy ending is a kind of stage play.

clue.text: Suitable country for vacation?

parts.note: split into a British short word for a holiday and a word for territory

explanation.definitionFit: The Netherlands, read as a land fit for a hol, British slang for a holiday.

clue.text: Give up and return

explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or concede; and the profit produced by an investment.

clue.text: Mean tooth could be taken out?

indicators.note: taken out suggests rearrangement, the fodder letters may be reordered

explanation.surface: A nasty molar fit for extraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be taken' rearranges MEAN TOOTH; 'out' doubles as part of the surface 'taken out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away from one's house, not in.
